A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SVBench and StreamingChat study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison after matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations, the single-instance versus multi-turn ablation, human comparisons, and runtime and model-size analyses in Tables 2–6 and Appendix F.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results, including StreamingChat evaluations, ablations, human comparisons, and appendix analyses.

M1.justification: The QA-chain construction and linking procedures and StreamingChat architecture and training procedure are unchanged. The newly reported leaderboard judge concerns evaluation, not the proposed model.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 1,353-video, 49,979-QA SVBench dataset, dialogue and streaming tasks, and nine skill categories. The MMBench, MMBench-Video, VideoMME, and MVBench evaluations are also retained; planned leaderboard updates establish no additional evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged across Tables 2–6, including the human, Flash-VStream, Qwen2-VL, and LLaVA-NeXT-Video comparisons already in v1. Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct is newly identified as a judge, not an evaluated competitor.

E3.justification: New Appendix G reports switching the ongoing leaderboard's scoring model from GPT-4o to Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct. This is a reported evaluation-protocol change; the PDFs do not establish that the existing tables were rerun. Previously documented splits, traversal procedures, and scoring criteria remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The single-instance versus multi-turn ablation, evaluator-versus-human comparison, runtime and memory analyses, model-size analysis, and Figures 11–15 case studies are retained. Their relocation adds no new analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same point-score reporting. Neither adds repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance-testing procedures.

E6.justification: Numerical entries in Tables 1–6 and the plotted and qualitative findings are unchanged. For example, StreamingChat's dialogue and streaming overall scores remain 59.41 and 53.90 in Table 2. Appendix G supplies no scores from the replacement judge.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions of QA chains, temporal relations, and modified linkages in Equations 1–4 are unchanged. Neither version introduces additional theorems, proofs, or formal assumptions.

C1.justification: The benchmark's novelty and scope and the main StreamingChat performance claims are retained. The introduction corrects the label attached to the existing 3.30% gain from dialogue to streaming, aligning the summary with the already reported streaming results.

C2.justification: Appendix G newly identifies the resource burden of GPT-4o scoring when evaluating many emerging models and uses this constraint to explain the judge replacement. Existing interpretations of model failures, contextual reasoning, human performance, and model-size effects are unchanged.

D1.justification: The abstract replaces the project-website access link with a GitHub repository link. Appendix G adds a leaderboard address and identifies its replacement scoring model. Existing implementation details and prompts are retained; the PDFs alone do not establish the linked resources' availability.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive related-work discussion are unchanged. Reformatting the related-work headings does not alter the paper's positioning or novelty claims.

P1.justification: v2 adds an Annotation Pipeline subsection, converts related-work subsections to paragraph headings, and inserts Appendix G, renumbering Prompts from G to H. It also corrects the introduction's evaluation label. The remaining prose is substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds gray highlighting to proposed-method or dataset rows in several tables and adjusts appendix layout. Table 5 moves from page 18 to 19, and Figure 11 moves from page 24 to 31. Figure content and table entries are retained.

improvement.justification: Correcting the headline evaluation label, clarifying the annotation-section hierarchy, and documenting the leaderboard's judge and access information modestly improve clarity and transparency. The scientific evidence remains unchanged, and no validation establishes that the replacement judge improves evaluation quality.
